[LSIG.7.2] A threshold crossing driven by a **new assertion** is reflected
immediately, on that assertion's evaluation. A crossing driven purely by the
**passage of time** — a quiet window sliding the value across the threshold —
is not self-triggering: the query returns a fresh value when evaluated, and
the engine evaluates at every pump ([LSER.8.1.1]). With no pump, the derived
fact does not change state, so the retraction latency of a fact whose source
can fall quiet is bounded by the host's pump interval. This is the same clock dependency
that `integral … gap hold` carries (§[LSIG.3.6]).
